answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks by tying identities to ionospheric scintillation. Nodes submit GNSS phase variations verified against ground receivers on an arid mesa, near a lotus wetland, and across an open tundra. Creating fake identities forces attackers to deploy discrete physical hardware across distant coordinates, imposing inescapable equipment and site costs. However, solar storms disrupt ionospheric stability, occasionally causing false rejections for honest nodes.
